messages.subject: rgeneric - log.prior
parts:
Dear all, 
Thank you for your time in advance. I am trying to build a rgeneric, I am using the code of the book "Bayesian Inference with INLA-Virgilio Gómez-Rubio" as a reference, con Chapter 11 the following code is presented for the log.prior function:

log.prior <- function() {
  param = interpret.theta()
  res <- dgamma(param$prec, 1, 5e-05, log = TRUE) + log(param$prec) +
      log(1) + log(param$rho) + log(1 - param$rho)
  return(res)
}

My questions are: 
  • Why do I need to specify the parameters highlight in yellow?
  • In the case of 3 prior that there need to be specified (2 for precision and 1 for correlation) is possible to:
 res <- dgamma(param$prec_1, 1, 5e-05, log = TRUE) + log(param$prec_1) +
dgamma(param$prec_2, 1, 5e-05, log = TRUE) + log(param$prec_2) +
      log(1) + log(param$rho) + log(1 - param$rho)

Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] rgeneric - log.prior
parts:
the internal representation is theta = log(precision)

you need to provide the log prior for theta.

if prec ~ Gamma(prec; a,b), then

pi(theta) = Gamma(prec=exp(theta); a, b) * |Jacobian|

and that is the 'magic' term on the first line. The rho term follows
similarly using the internal representation of the correlation.



H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] rgeneric - log.prior
parts:
the internal representation is theta = log(precision)

you need to provide the log prior for theta.

if prec ~ Gamma(prec; a,b), then

pi(theta) = Gamma(prec=exp(theta); a, b) * |Jacobian|

and that is the 'magic' term on the first line. The rho term follows
similarly using the internal representation of the correlation.

In addition to this, please check section 5.3.1 on defining new priors as this is related to your question:

https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/inla-gitbook/ch-priors.html#sec:newpriors

You will find Table 5.3 with several internal representations that are used quite often and the terms that you need to add to the log-prior in the internal scale.

Best,

Virgilio
